newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Koncar sees 1996 profit little changed.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Koncar sees 1996 profit little changed.

text.p: The Croatian electrical giant Koncar said on Friday it expects this year's net profit to be little changed from the consolidated profit posted in 1995.

"The profit will be on roughly the same level. It may just catch up with last year's or be in the region of 14 million kuna ($2.6 million)," Ivan Cesarec, assistant to the chief executive, told Reuters by telephone.
It made a group profit of 14.7 million kuna last year as costs were slashed, up from 1994's 4.65 million, despite a decline in overall sales to 868 million from 945 million kuna.
But Cesarec said Koncar's final results would not reflect an expected 6-7 percent increase in sales as some parts of the group would end the year with production losses.
"One company suffered a big setback in orders and its loss will have to be covered by other (subsidiaries)," he said.
Some of Koncar's units had large army orders, which have shrunk since the end of conflicts in former Yugoslavia in 1995.
This year the group hopes to have almost 700 million kuna sales in Croatia, with exports nearing 500 million.
The government owns more than 60 percent of Koncar and several foreign firms including Germany's Siemens and Saudi firm Nesma have stakes in it.
Koncar is one of the most likely candidates for future sell-off through a foreign offering.
It plans to list its shares in Zagreb and London bourses in about a year's time.
-- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075 ($ = 5.439 Croatian Kuna)
